tls.implementation: node:tls on OpenSSL (X25519MLKEM768 and X25519 groups)
tls.certificateSignature: ECDSA P-256 with SHA-256 (classical; identical in both conditions)
tls.resumption: disabled: every handshake is a full handshake (no session tickets, no reuse)

workload.label: ^dev^ laptop,^ loopback,^ standard^ preset^
workload.connectionReuse: none (new TCP connection and full handshake every time)

measurement.interleaving: classical-first on even runs, hybrid-first on odd runs
measurement.statistics: linear-interpolated percentiles (R-7); bootstrap CIs resample independent RUNS (2000 resamples, recorded seed), not individual handshakes

capture.packetCapture: none retained; handshake sizes come from the plaintext ClientHello/ServerHello record lengths observed on the socket
capture.handshakeByteSource: wire bytes counted by the tap stream up to handshake completion, both directions

caveats: Single host over loopback: latencies are not representative of any production or partner network.
Client and server share one machine's CPU; contention is possible and run-to-run variation is reported, not hidden.
Handshake timing excludes TCP connection setup and application data.
Per-handshake CPU time comes from process.cpuUsage(), whose resolution is coarse on some platforms (notably Windows); treat CPU figures as averages over many handshakes, noisy at small sample sizes.
The results characterise this implementation (Node.js/OpenSSL) in this environment only.
